title: What If Betelgeuse Exploded Tonight?

scenes.text: What if Betelgeuse exploded tonight? You'd see it in broad daylight, and nothing bad would happen.
The star is hundreds of light-years away, so it may already have exploded. We'd only see it when the light arrives.
At its peak it would shine about as bright as a half Moon, for more than three months.
It would stay visible in the daytime sky for about a year, and at night for several years.
Radiation is the real danger, but only from a few dozen light-years. Betelgeuse is far beyond that. Life on Earth would be unharmed.
It could happen any time in the next hundred thousand years. Detectors might give us a day's warning.

description:
What if Betelgeuse exploded tonight?
It would shine like a half Moon for three months and be visible in daylight, yet Earth would be safe.
